user_text: Summarize the benefits of code review for a small team.
assistant_text:
# Benefits of Code Review for a Small Team

## Quality & Reliability
- **Catches bugs early** before they reach production, reducing costly fixes later
- **Enforces consistency** in coding style and standards across the codebase

## Knowledge Sharing
- **Spreads expertise** so no single person is the only one who understands a feature
- **Onboards new members faster** by exposing them to existing patterns and practices
- **Reduces bus factor** — the risk of losing critical knowledge if someone leaves

## Collaboration & Communication
- **Encourages team discussion** around design decisions and trade-offs
- **Builds a shared sense of ownership** over the codebase

## Learning & Growth
- **Junior developers improve faster** through feedback from more experienced teammates
- **Senior developers stay sharp** by explaining and justifying their decisions

## Practical Advantages for Small Teams
| Benefit | Why It Matters |
|---|---|
| Fewer production incidents | Less time firefighting |
| Better documentation habits | Code is easier to maintain long-term |
| Accountability | Everyone writes with the expectation of review |

## Key Consideration
Code review works best when feedback is **constructive and specific** — small teams especially benefit from keeping reviews collaborative rather than critical.

> Even a lightweight review process (one reviewer, async comments) delivers significant returns for small teams.
Code review helps small teams catch bugs early, share knowledge, and maintain a consistent, high-quality codebase.

1. **Bug detection** — Reviewers catch errors before code reaches production, saving time and reducing costly fixes.
2. **Knowledge sharing** — Team members learn from each other's feedback, preventing knowledge silos and reducing dependency on any one person.
Code review builds a **shared sense of ownership**, encouraging everyone on the team to take responsibility for the quality of the entire codebase rather than just their own contributions.

user_text: State one risk if reviews are skipped.
assistant_text: If code reviews are skipped, **knowledge silos can form**, leaving critical parts of the codebase understood by only one person — creating a serious risk if that person leaves or is unavailable.
Track **defect escape rate** — the percentage of bugs that make it to production — which should decrease over time if code reviews are effective.
Even a simple, lightweight review process can significantly improve code quality and team cohesion over time.

• Code review catches bugs early and improves overall code quality.
• It promotes knowledge sharing and reduces dependency on any one team member.
• A consistent review process builds team ownership and accountability.
• Tracking defect escape rate helps measure its effectiveness.
• Even a lightweight process delivers meaningful long-term benefits.
Code review is a simple but powerful practice that keeps small teams aligned, informed, and shipping better software.
Code review is only effective if feedback is kept constructive and timely — overly critical or delayed reviews can slow progress and harm team morale.
Constructive, timely feedback makes code review effective; criticism harms morale.
Code review helps small teams catch bugs, share knowledge, and maintain quality — but only when feedback is constructive and consistent.
